schema_notes: `required` is tri-state: true = the command cannot act without the key on any path; false = optional on every path; "conditional" = required only inside a branch, the branch named in the key's `notes` and in the command's `branches`.

`branches` (unit-1 field, kept) -- every handler in this unit except the nine variable commands is selector-shaped (`action`, then a per-action sub-selector like `target`): a flat required/optional split would misstate them.
`value_docs` (unit-1 field, kept) -- where a key is enumerated and each value selects a different effect, C6's per-thing doc line is attached per value.

`key_grammar` (unit-1 field, kept) -- for the ten commands whose key is not from a fixed list: define/add/sub/multiply/divide/modulo/tangent/trunc/sinus (key = a variable name) and the `struct` loop/if forms are NOT of that shape (struct's keys are fixed and appear in `args`).

`downstream` (unit-1 field, kept, boolean) -- key not read in this line range: the handler forwards the whole `args` map and the key is read in another file. Anchored there. Such keys consume NO row of the count gate.

Absent-key value for every eval* conversion is fixed IN the handler file and is not opaque: evalDouble("")=0.0, evalInt("")=0, evalString("")="" -- and the three functions PHYSICALLY LIVE IN THIS UNIT'S RANGE (app_command_interface.cpp:4458-4479, no `args[` inside them, so they consume no count-gate row). What a NON-empty string evaluates to stays opaque here (app_command_eval.cpp, INTENT S5 item 5): recorded as evalDouble/evalInt/evalString, $-variable substitution possible. EXCEPTION, recorded because this unit is where it is decided: the nine variable commands hand their pair to app_command_eval directly, so their SEMANTICS are that file's; the key/value GRAMMAR (which key is legal, what the value may be) is read from it here only far enough to state the key domain, per DoD 4 (no invention) -- the arithmetic itself is anchored, not re-derived.

body.doc: Act on the objects of a star system: add one, remove one, hide it, recolour it, or change how it is drawn.

action.doc: What to do; every other key on the line depends on this word.

value_docs.load: Add an object. With `mode` it adds a three-dimensional model file (see `mode`); without it, it adds a body to the star system, described by the same keys a system data file uses.
value_docs.remove: Remove one three-dimensional model, by `name`, from the scene named by `mode` (this value is only read on the model path).
value_docs.clear: With `mode`: remove every model from that scene. Without `mode`: remove every body a script has added, keeping the ones the data file declared.
value_docs.drop: Remove the one body called `name` (only bodies a script added can be removed).
value_docs.initial: Put every body back to the state its data file declared, and show or hide it as that file said.
value_docs.reload: Read the current system's data file again, keeping where you stand and what time it is: edits to the file take effect, bodies removed from it disappear, bodies added to it appear.
value_docs.save: Write the current system to a system file, so that the bodies a script pushed in this session are ordinary data at the next start.
value_docs.preload: Fetch a body's big picture files into memory now, so that arriving there later does not stall (see `keep_time` and `purge`).
value_docs.dual_dump: Development tool: write a machine-readable record of both drawing paths' state to a file.
value_docs.screenshot: Take a picture of the screen through the program's own capture path (development tool).

value_docs.in_galaxy: the scene drawn when you are inside the galaxy

filename.doc: The file to read or write, depending on the action.
filename.default: on the model form: absent -> the built name is "/.ojm" and no model is found; on `action save`: absent -> this system's own file; on `action dual_dump`: absent -> /tmp/dual_trace.json; on `action screenshot`: absent -> an automatic name <base>-YY.MM.DD-HH.MM.SS.png

notes: Order of the forms, which decides what a mixed line does: model form (needs `mode` AND `action`), then `skin_use`, then `skin_tex`, then `action`, then `name`, then `tesselation` (:4028, :4048, :4058, :4063, :4100, :4184). `body action load skin_use on` therefore only switches the picture.

`action drop` with no `name` does NOT report a missing name: the test is `argAction == W_DROP && argName != ""` (:4070), so the line falls through to "command 'body' : unknown action argument" (:4094) -- the same misleading-message shape unit 1 recorded for `dso`.

A `mode` value outside the three words with a valid system `action` silently takes the SYSTEM path (the test at :4028 fails and `mode` is then never looked at again) -- e.g. `body mode in_galaxie action clear` removes every script-added BODY instead of the models of a scene.

DEFECT, recorded not fixed, same class as unit 1's `color`: on the r/g/b path the colour helper writes its range errors into a BY-VALUE copy of debug_message (src/interfaceModule/app_command_color.cpp:58-59), so `body name X color halo r 2 g 0 b 0` changes nothing, reports success and is recorded. The hex and rgb-word paths set the message on the reference and do reach the script (src/interfaceModule/app_command_color.cpp:98-105, 112-119).

C1-relevant: this is the handler that WRITES into the parsed map (`path` :4066, `tex_ring` :4068, `keep_time` :4085-4086) and then forwards the whole map (:4069, :4087). A tool that models 'the keys of this line' must not read them back from the downstream side.

DOC-vs-CODE divergence recorded, code wins: two engine-side comments spell the colour form as `body name X color <halo|label|orbit|trail|all> value r,g,b` (src/experimentalModule/BodyModule.hpp:49 @ b45d3b58 [NOT AT HEAD: the comment that spelled the colour form left the code] and :264 @ b45d3b58 [NOT AT HEAD: the comment that spelled the colour form left the code]), but the handler reads `color_value` (:4137) -- `value` on a `body` line means the tesselation number and nothing else (:4185). An author following the header comment would silently set no colour.
flagged: body downstream vocabulary (`action load` without `mode`): the forwarded map is read by the stellar-system-file body grammar (src/bodyModule/protosystem.cpp:499-813 and the new path's loaders), which is INTENT S5 item 4's own deliverable -- the second contract file. Enumerating it here would duplicate that authority (I2). Recorded instead: the entry points (other_args_uses:4069) and the four keys the immediate downstream names before anything else (name, parent, coord_func, type). SCOPE DECISION, for the supervisor to confirm or reverse.

camera.doc: Move the point of view about the universe: name a place, go to it, turn towards a body, or fly up from where you stand.

action.doc: What to do with the point of view; every other key on the line depends on this word.

value_docs.rotate: turn the view towards the place you are standing on, over `duration` seconds
value_docs.align_with: tilt the view so that the named place's own up direction becomes yours, over `duration` seconds
value_docs.transition_to: change what the view is attached to, without travelling: either the place you stand right now, or a body
value_docs.move_to: travel to a point of space or to a body, over `duration`
value_docs.save: write where the view is, and when, into a file
value_docs.load: put the view back where such a file says
value_docs.free_mode: switch free flight on or off
value_docs.descend: go down towards, or up away from, what you are looking at
value_docs.move_lat: keep moving in latitude at the speed `value` gives, -1 to 1 (the sign is the direction), until the next `move_lat`; `value 0` stops
value_docs.move_lon: keep moving in longitude at the speed `value` gives, -1 to 1 (the sign is the direction), until the next `move_lon`; `value 0` stops
value_docs.raise_height: keep rising at the speed `value` gives, 0 to 1, until the next height order; `value 0` stops a rise
value_docs.lower_height: keep descending at the speed `value` gives, 0 to 1, until the next height order; `value 0` stops a descent
value_docs.lift_off: climb to a given height and then detach the view from the body

value_docs.switch: attach the view to a named place

name.doc: The name of a place the view can be attached to (its own name, not a body's).
name.default: absent -> the four forms that need it are refused with "command 'camera' : missing name", which is ALSO what an unknown action reports
name.notes: On `action transition_to target body` the same key means a BODY name instead (:4293) -- the only place in this handler where it does.

value_docs.point: on `transition_to`: the exact place you are standing right now becomes a named place called temp_point; on `move_to`: the point given by `x`, `y` and `z`
value_docs.body: a body: named by `name` on `transition_to`, by `body_name` on `move_to`

target.default: absent -> "command 'camera' : missing target" (rotate: "missing target"; transition_to and move_to: their own message); present with any other word -> "command 'transition_to' : unknown target arg" / "command 'camera' : unknown target arg"

duration.doc: How long the movement takes, in seconds.
duration.default: on `rotate`: absent -> 2 seconds; on `align_with`: absent -> 0 (immediate); on `move_to target point`: absent -> the jump is immediate; on `move_to target body`: absent -> "command 'move_to body' : missing a body_name or time"; on `lift_off`: absent -> 3 seconds
duration.notes: On both `move_to` forms the script ALSO waits: the delay before the next command is set to this many seconds (:4337, :4366 -- evalInt(value) x 1000 milliseconds, so a fractional duration is cut down to whole seconds for the wait but not for the movement). The travel itself is measured in simulated time: the seconds are divided by 86400 and the arrival is that many days later on the simulation clock (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:430, 464).

body.doc: On `action align_with`, the name of the place (declared with `action create`, of the kind that follows a body) whose up direction the view should take.
body.notes: Despite the key name it is looked up among the declared PLACES, not among the bodies, and the place must be one that follows a body; otherwise the log says "anchor not found" / "wrong anchor type" and the command reports "error align_with_body body".

body_name.doc: On `action move_to target body`, which body to travel to.
body_name.default: absent -> "command 'move_to body' : missing a body_name or time"
body_name.notes: As with `body` above, the name is looked up among the declared PLACES that follow a body (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:491-497), so only bodies that have such a place declared can be travelled to.

x.doc: On `action move_to target point`, where to go: the first coordinate, counted from the Sun.
x.notes: The three numbers are a position in the heliocentric ecliptic frame (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:387-395, 405-442). The unit is NOT stated on this path: astronomical units is [derived] from two facts about the same frame -- the km->AU divisor applied to `altitude` beside it (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:475, with AU declared in kilometres at src/tools/sc_const.hpp:45), and the new-path anchor code, which says 'a fixed point x/y/z in AU' of the same coordinates (src/experimentalModule/CameraAnchors.cpp:100). z.doc: On `action move_to target point`, where to go: the third coordinate, counted from the Sun.

values: on-forms per Utility::isTrue = free flight on
state.notes: Same silent-off class as `flag`: a typo means 'off' with no diagnostic. New drawing path only.

coef.doc: On `action descend`, how much closer to go: less than 1 goes down, more than 1 goes up (0.5 halves the distance, 2 doubles it).
coef.notes: What it goes down towards depends on where you are: the ground under the view ray when a body is close, the last selected body when you are out among the systems (src/experimentalModule/Camera.cpp:728-742). New drawing path only.

value.doc: On `action follow_rotation`, whether the view turns with the body: write exactly the word true for yes; on the four held moves (`move_lat`, `move_lon`, `raise_height`, `lower_height`), how fast to keep moving.
value.value: on `follow_rotation`: string compared literally against "true"; on `move_lat`, `move_lon`, `raise_height` and `lower_height`: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible
value.default: on `follow_rotation`: absent -> no; on `move_lat`, `move_lon`, `raise_height` and `lower_height`: absent -> "command 'camera <action>' : missing value"

On `move_lat`, `move_lon`, `raise_height` and `lower_height` the number is an order HELD until the next one on its axis: each frame the engine adds the joystick's push to it, keeps the sum within -1 to 1 and moves by its cube (src/coreModule/core.cpp:1937-1962), so a number beyond the bounds acts as the bound; `raise_height` and `lower_height` share ONE order, the later replacing the earlier, `value 0` on one of them stops only its own direction, and with no range check a negative number on either moves the other way (src/coreModule/core.cpp:1810-1824).

tilt the view to that place's up direction; failure gives "error align_with_body body"

write the view's place, height, date and direction to a file; failure gives "error saving camera"
read such a file back; failure gives "error loading CameraAnchor"
switch free flight on or off
go down towards, or up away from, what you look at
keep moving in latitude at that speed (-1 to 1) until the next `move_lat`, `value 0` stops; a missing value gives "command 'camera move_lat' : missing value"
keep moving in longitude at that speed (-1 to 1) until the next `move_lon`, `value 0` stops; a missing value gives "command 'camera move_lon' : missing value"

notes: The `name` test at :4466 sits between the two groups of actions: every action listed before it works without a name, every one after it needs one -- and any UNKNOWN action word is reported as a missing name when none was written, which is a misleading message for a misspelt action.

C1-relevant: `action lift_off` does not act itself -- it builds a three-line script (moveto / wait / camera action transition_to target point) and pushes it in front of the running script (:4457-4463). Those three lines are parsed by ScriptMgr::addScriptFirst (src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:81-107), whose comment rule differs from the file loader's: there an INDENTED '#' IS dropped as a comment (src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:90-97), while at the script-file layer only a '#' in the first column is (src/scriptModule/script.cpp:117, parse_model.comments).

C1-relevant: `action lift_off` returns addScriptFirst's value directly (:4463) instead of executeCommandStatus(), so the line is never recorded by the recorder and never reports a failure -- addScriptFirst always returns true (src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:106).

`action create` forwards the whole parsed map (:4473) to TWO registries which read DIFFERENT vocabularies for the same declaration: the old one accepts type point/observatory/body/orbit with x/y/z, body_name, parent, orbit_center_* (src/navModule/anchor_creator_cor.cpp), the new one the same plus follow_rotation and the orbit keys, and refuses with an explaining log line (src/experimentalModule/CameraAnchors.cpp:79-104). The command reports success when EITHER registry accepted (src/bodyModule/ssystem_factory.hpp:642-647).

`action rotate`, `align_with`, `move_to target body` and `align_with` all look their name up among the DECLARED PLACES, not among the bodies: without a place declared for a body (by `action create`, or by the anchor file the program reads at start), those forms cannot reach it.

define.doc: Give a name to a value so that later commands can use it instead of writing the number again.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name you choose for the value, the VALUE is what it holds.
key_grammar.key_domain: any word EXCEPT the 24 reserved names (families.reserved_variables): a reserved name is refused with the message "<name> is a reservedVar so you can't define it" written to the program's standard output, and nothing is stored
key_grammar.value: a number, or the name of another variable (its value is copied), or the name of a reserved variable (its current value is copied), or any other text (stored as text, counting as 0 in arithmetic)
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "Unexpected error in command_define" (note that `define x` is no pair: a key with no value is dropped by the parser, parse_model.pair_extraction)

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, and it is the ALPHABETICALLY FIRST key of the line, not the first written: the handler reads args.begin() and never loops (:4539-4541). `define b 2 a 1` defines only `a`. Confirms parse_model.flag_multi_pair's list.

How the value is read (src/interfaceModule/app_command_eval.cpp:143-157): a reserved name gives that reading's current value; an existing variable name gives that variable's value; otherwise the text is converted to a number, and if it is not a number at all it is kept as text with the numeric value 0.
The variables live until the program stops or a script ends (AppCommandInterface::deleteVar, :120-123); `struct print var` lists them.

add.doc: Add a number to a named value.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name of the value to change, the VALUE is the number to add to it.
key_grammar.key_domain: a name given earlier by `define`, or one of the four reserved names that can be written (longitude, latitude, altitude, heading -- families.reserved_variables); a name that was never defined is CREATED and set to the value written, with the log line "Not possible to operate with undefined variable so define to null from ops"
key_grammar.value: number, or the name of another variable (its value is used)
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command_addition"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4553-4555) -- the handler even says so: '// could loop if want to allow that syntax' (:4552).

Writing to a reserved name works for the four that have a setter (longitude, latitude, altitude, heading); the others log "No setter with reserved variable <name>. Do nothing." (src/interfaceModule/app_command_eval.cpp:348-376).

Reserved names take a SECOND path in the same call: after the reserved value is written the code falls on to the ordinary-variable branch, which does not find the name and tries to define it -- which is refused, printing "<name> is a reservedVar so you can't define it" (src/interfaceModule/app_command_eval.cpp:205-214 then :137-141). The arithmetic still happened.

sub.doc: Take a number away from a named value.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name of the value to change, the VALUE is the number to take away.
key_grammar.value: number, or the name of another variable
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command_substract"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4566-4568). Reserved-name behaviour as `add`.

multiply.doc: Multiply a named value by a number.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name of the value to change, the VALUE is what to multiply it by.
key_grammar.value: number, or the name of another variable
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command__multiply"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4580-4582). Reserved-name behaviour as `add`.

divide.doc: Divide a named value by a number.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name of the value to change, the VALUE is what to divide it by.
key_grammar.value: number, or the name of another variable
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command__divide"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4593-4595). Reserved-name behaviour as `add`.
Nothing checks for a zero divisor: the division is plain floating-point, so dividing by 0 stores an infinite value (src/interfaceModule/app_command_eval.cpp:10).

modulo.doc: Replace a named value by what is left over after dividing it by a number.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name of the value to change, the VALUE is the number to divide by.
key_grammar.value: number, or the name of another variable
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command__modulo"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4606-4608). The remainder is the floating-point one (std::fmod), so it works with values that are not whole numbers. Reserved-name behaviour as `add`.

tangent.doc: Put the tangent of an angle into a named value.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name that RECEIVES the result, the VALUE is the angle in degrees.
key_grammar.key_domain: as `add` -- but note the name's current value is not used at all, it is overwritten
key_grammar.value: number of degrees, or the name of another variable
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command__tangent"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4619-4621).

Unlike add/sub/multiply/divide/modulo this is NOT a two-sided operation: the function ignores the variable's current value and stores the tangent of the value written (src/interfaceModule/app_command_eval.cpp:12). The angle is in degrees, converted with 3.1415926 (a shortened value of pi, so results carry a small error).

trunc.doc: Put a number, with everything after its decimal point cut off, into a named value.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name that RECEIVES the result, the VALUE is the number to cut.
key_grammar.key_domain: as `add` -- the name's current value is not used, it is overwritten
key_grammar.value: number, or the name of another variable
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command__trunc"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4632-4634). Cutting is towards zero: -2.7 becomes -2.

sinus.doc: Put the sine of an angle into a named value.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name that RECEIVES the result, the VALUE is the angle in degrees.
key_grammar.key_domain: as `add` -- the name's current value is not used, it is overwritten
key_grammar.value: number of degrees, or the name of another variable
key_grammar.default: no pair at all -> debug_message "unexpected error in command__sinus"

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, alphabetically first key (:4645-4647). Degrees, converted with the same shortened pi as `tangent`.

struct.doc: Control which lines of the script run: ask a question and skip what follows when the answer is no, repeat a block, or switch a block off.

if.doc: Open a block that only runs when a condition holds; also closes or flips such a block.

value_docs.else: flip the block: what was skipped now runs and the other way round
value_docs.end: close the block opened by the last `struct if`
value_docs.<number>: with one of the comparison keys below, the left-hand side of the comparison; alone, the block runs when this is NOT zero

if.default: absent -> the command tries `comment`, then `loop`, then `print`
if.notes: Blocks may be nested; each `struct if` must be closed by `struct if end` (an `end` or an `else` with no open block is reported as an error on its own line and ignored -- src/interfaceModule/app_command_interface.cpp:4661-4670).

equal.doc: Run the block when the `if` value is the same as this one.
equal.default: absent -> the next comparison key is tried
equal.notes: The two numbers count as the same when they differ by less than 0.0001 (:4657, :4672).

diff.doc: Run the block when the `if` value is NOT the same as this one.
diff.default: absent -> the next comparison key is tried

inf.doc: Run the block when the `if` value is smaller than this one.
inf.default: absent -> the next comparison key is tried

inf_equal.doc: Run the block when the `if` value is smaller than this one or the same.
inf_equal.default: absent -> the next comparison key is tried

sup.doc: Run the block when the `if` value is bigger than this one.
sup.default: absent -> the next comparison key is tried

sup_equal.doc: Run the block when the `if` value is bigger than this one or the same.
sup_equal.default: absent -> no comparison key is left: the block then runs when the `if` value is not zero

comment.doc: Switch off the lines that follow (yes), or switch them back on (no).
values: on-forms per Utility::isTrue = stop executing what follows
ANYTHING ELSE = start executing again, silently
comment.notes: Exactly the same switch as the `comment` and `uncomment` commands (parse_model.comments.block_form); skipped lines are logged "this command has not been executed" (:323). Same silent-off class as `flag`.

loop.doc: Repeat the lines that follow a given number of times, or close/abandon such a repetition.
loop.value: int(via evalString then Utility::strToInt) -- $-variable substitution possible | enumerated

value_docs.end: close the repeated block: go back to its first line and run it again until the count is used up
value_docs.break: abandon the repetition altogether, right now
value_docs.<number>: start a block to be run that many times; 0 or less runs it no times at all (the lines are skipped until `struct loop end`)

loop.source: app_command_interface.cpp:4732-4766 -> src/scriptModule/script_interface.cpp:81-83, 93-99, 121-123 -> src/scriptModule/script_mgr.hpp:132-147, src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:269-276, 311-339 (W_LOOP="loop", W_BREAK="break", W_END="end": base_command_interface.hpp:165 (also 284), 171, 157)
loop.notes: A count of exactly 1 does nothing at all (:4758-4765 acts only below 1 and above 1), which is the same as running the block once. The repetition only works for lines coming from a script FILE: the lines are collected as the file is read (src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:332-333), so commands sent over the network are not repeated. This key is IGNORED while a `struct if` block is being skipped (:4733).

print.doc: Write the list of named values and what they hold into the script log.
print.default: absent or any other word -> nothing is written
print.notes: The names are written in alphabetical order, one per line, between two marker lines; with no names defined the line written is "Not variable available".

branches.selector: if present (and no `comment` block is switched off)
branches.effect: open, flip or close a conditional block; the FIRST comparison key present decides, in the order equal, diff, inf, inf_equal, sup, sup_equal; with none, the block runs when the `if` value is not zero
switch the following lines off or on

branches.selector: loop present (and not inside a skipped `if` block)
branches.effect: start, close or abandon a repetition
list the named values in the log
no debug_message is ever set: the command reports SUCCESS having done nothing

notes: RECONCILIATION with parse_model.pre_table_commands (the unit-4 assignment). `struct` IS both intercepted before the table (:318-319) and registered (app_command_init.cpp:90) -- but the two paths are not equivalent: (a) the interception happens BEFORE the skip test at :230, which is why a `struct` line still runs inside a switched-off or skipped block -- without that, no `struct if end` could ever close a block it is inside; (b) the REGISTERED path is dead code: the switch case for SC_STRUCT is an empty `break;` labelled '// for g++ warning' (:401), so reaching the table with the command `struct` would do nothing -- and it cannot be reached anyway, since the literal test at :318 already caught it. What the registration actually buys is presence in the did-you-mean list and in the enum-to-name map used by the recorder (app_command_init.cpp:99-112). REFINES the parse_model line, which today says only 'struct is also registered'.

The `if` branch is guarded by `swapCommand != true` (:4660): inside a block switched off by `comment` (or by `struct comment true`), conditional lines are ignored -- but `struct comment false` still works, since the `comment` branch has no such guard. This is what makes a switched-off block closable.

The `if` branch is NOT guarded by the if-skip state, which is what makes nesting work: every `struct if` inside a skipped block still pushes a level, so its own `end` pops the right one (src/interfaceModule/if_swap.cpp:57-62, 90-99).
A block is skipped when ANY enclosing level says skip (src/interfaceModule/if_swap.cpp:90-99), so a false outer condition cannot be undone by a true inner one.
The `loop` branch does NOT return when the count is exactly 1, so such a line falls through to the `print` test (:4761-4768) -- the only path in the handler where two branches can act on one line.

random.doc: Set the range that the built-in chance value is drawn from.

min.doc: The smallest number the chance value may take.

max.doc: The largest number the chance value may take.

branches.effect: set one or both ends of the range; both may be given on one line
debug_message "unknown random parameter"

notes: This is the one command of the unit that reads TWO keys of its own and acts on both: at least one of them must be there.

The range is used by the reserved name `random` (families.reserved_variables), which gives a new evenly-drawn number between the two ends every time it is read (src/interfaceModule/app_command_eval.cpp:338-339). Nothing checks that min is below max.

transition.doc: Control the smooth fades the program plays when something appears or disappears: let them finish at once, freeze them, or let them run again.

action.doc: What to do with the fades.

value_docs.skip: jump the fades forward by `duration` so that they are over now
value_docs.pause: freeze every fade where it is

action.default: absent or any other word -> "command 'transition': unknown argument"
action.notes: C1-relevant: read with std::move (:4796), so the map entry is left empty for the rest of the command -- the only handler in the unit that empties a key it read.

duration.doc: On `action skip`, how much fade time to jump through, in thousandths of a second.
duration.default: absent or 0 -> 3600 (the code's own comment: "Ensure transitions complete now")
duration.source: app_command_interface.cpp:4798-4806 -> src/coreModule/core.cpp:2701-2707 (Core::update takes delta_time in milliseconds: 'const float deltaSeconds = delta_time / 1000.f') (W_DURATION="duration", base_command_interface.hpp:102)
duration.notes: The number is passed as the time step of one update, so it is in milliseconds -- 3600 is 3.6 seconds of fade time. It reaches an `int` parameter, so anything after the decimal point is dropped.

branches.effect: jump the fades forward; when fades are frozen they are briefly allowed to run so the jump takes effect, then frozen again
freeze every fade
let the fades run again
"command 'transition': unknown argument"

notes: `action skip` while the fades are frozen does NOT leave them running: the handler switches them on, does the jump and switches them off again (:4801-4805).
The jump advances both drawing paths' fades in one call (src/coreModule/core.cpp:2701-2707).
flagged: transition.duration unit: the code answers 'milliseconds' (Core::update's parameter), but the default of 3600 is commented "Ensure transitions complete now", which only holds for fades shorter than 3.6 seconds -- the two readings (a millisecond step, or a seconds value that was meant) do not agree. The doc line states what the code does. Whether the intent was seconds is not answerable from the code: Vixy.

c1_parse_model: REFINES parse_model.pre_table_commands: `struct` is intercepted at :318-319 BEFORE the skip test at :322 (which is what lets `struct if end` / `struct comment false` close a block they are inside), and its REGISTERED path is dead -- `case SC_COMMAND::SC_STRUCT: break;` (:401) calls nothing. The registration's only live effects are the did-you-mean list and the recorder's enum-to-name map (app_command_init.cpp:90, 99-112). Suggested wording for the merge: 'struct is also registered, but only for the did-you-mean list and the recorder: the table's own case does nothing, and the literal test always catches the line first.'

ADDS a second comment grammar, reachable from this unit: `camera action lift_off` pushes a three-line script through ScriptMgr::addScriptFirst (src/scriptModule/script_mgr.cpp:81-107), which strips leading whitespace and treats an INDENTED '#' as a comment -- the opposite of the script-file layer's column-0-only rule (src/scriptModule/script.cpp:117). scedit's model of 'what is a comment' must be per-channel: file layer (column 0 only), addScriptFirst layer (first non-blank character), live channels (never stripped).

CONFIRMS the eval boundary recorded by unit 1 and locates it: evalString/evalDouble/evalInt are at app_command_interface.cpp:4513-4534, inside THIS unit's range, and hold the absent-key defaults ("", 0.0, 0). They contain no `args[` and so consume no count-gate row.

ADDS a boolean-grammar exception for the vocabulary model: `camera action follow_rotation value <v>` is an exact string comparison against "true" (:4498), not the flag grammar -- `on`, `1` and `TRUE` all mean NO there. Every other boolean of the unit is isTrue/isFalse/toggle. A lint rule that assumes flag grammar for every boolean-looking value would be wrong here.
